name: Why do mobile home drywall seams and corners keep cracking?

mainEntity.name: Why do mobile home drywall seams and corners keep cracking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cracks in mobile home drywall frequently stem from foundation movement, shifting piers, or ground changes. Unlike standard site-built homes with continuous concrete foundations, manufactured homes sit on piers, tie-downs, or blocks that can shift as ground moisture changes across seasonal freeze-thaw cycles. When the home settles unevenly, stress concentrates at interior door frames, window corners, and wall seams. If you notice wide or recurring drywall cracks, have your home's leveling and pier supports inspected before repairing the drywall, or the cracks will simply reappear after patching.
acceptedAnswer.description: Cracking usually happens when the home shifts on its pier or block foundation due to seasonal ground movement, concentrating stress at panel joints and openings.
